{"PREMISE":"# The Last Lantern

## Player proposition

You are Mara Venn, a harbour maintenance runner in the storm-walled city of
Breakwater. When essential machinery fails, you reach it before the weather does.

## Intended experience

A short solo industrial adventure about practical problem-solving, investigation,
and choosing who should bear the cost of keeping a city alive. Expect one clear job,
a small location, three people with competing interests, and several viable solutions.

## Campaign loop

Receive a municipal job, prepare, enter a hazardous site, discover the human problem
inside the mechanical one, and decide what repair or compromise to leave behind.
","SETTING":"# Breakwater

## Player knowledge

Breakwater occupies a chain of concrete islands behind an immense storm wall. Cargo,
food, medicine, and passengers cross the flooded outer districts by rail ferry. Beacon
lanterns guide those ferries through reefs and half-submerged buildings.

Municipal maintenance runners are licensed to enter service sites, requisition common
parts, and make emergency repairs. They are competent workers, not police. Dockworkers
and municipal crews are exhausted after months of automation cuts and worsening storms.

## Factions

The Harbour Office keeps traffic moving with too little money and treats delay as the
greatest danger. The Dock Union protects skilled workers and distrusts automation. North
Channel Freight owns several ferries but depends on public beacons and municipal crews.

## Useful technology

Beacon lanterns combine an electric arc, rotating mirror, radio identifier, and manual
chemical flare. Maintenance equipment is rugged and comprehensible. Local terminals
keep timestamped fault and access records. Radios work poorly inside reinforced tunnels.

## Director-only truths

No faction is secretly omnipotent. Infrastructure failures have physical causes, records
can be incomplete without lying, and ordinary workers retain agency under pressure.
","RULES":"# Rules

## Character creation

This playtest uses the pregenerated character in `characters/mara-venn.md`.

## Declaring actions

Describe what Mara attempts and, when relevant, the approach or equipment she uses.
Routine movement, inspection, conversation, and competent maintenance succeed without
a roll unless immediate pressure creates an interesting consequence.

## Checks

Roll a d20 only when an action is uncertain, consequential, and has an interesting
failure. Difficulty is 10 for pressured, 14 for hard, or 18 for severe. Apply +2 for a
clearly relevant strength or preparation and -2 for a relevant hindrance. Meeting the
difficulty succeeds; exceeding it by at least 5 is a strong success. Natural 1 and 20
are critical failure and critical success.

Failure changes position, consumes time or equipment, creates danger, or forces a hard
choice. It never makes the player repeat the same action until a roll succeeds.

## Harm and recovery

Describe harm fictionally. Minor harm impairs an immediately relevant action. Serious
harm ends unsafe exertion until Mara receives help. Failure never kills Mara without a
previously stated mortal risk and a meaningful chance to avoid it.

## Equipment

Ordinary equipment works as expected. A listed item may enable an approach, avoid a
check, justify +2, or be consumed to prevent a consequence. Do not invent ammunition,
battery, or paperwork chores unless the Screamsheet establishes them as meaningful.

## Time and pressure

Pressure advances because Mara spends significant fictional time, triggers an event, or
gives another actor a credible opportunity to act. It does not advance once per message.
","BOUNDARIES":"# Boundaries

## Tone

Grounded, tense, humane industrial science fiction. Machinery should feel physical and
repairable. People may be frightened, stubborn, compromised, or angry without becoming
caricatures.

## Content boundaries

No sexual violence, torture, cruelty to children, graphic injury, or unavoidable death.
Do not frame poverty, labour action, or technical ignorance as moral failure.

## Presentation

Use concise second-person prose. Make exits, hazards, useful objects, and changes in the
situation perceptible. Do not hide basic setting knowledge Mara would possess. End each
resolved turn with a concrete changed situation rather than a menu of suggested actions.
","SCREAMSHEET":"# Beacon Seven

## Player pitch

Beacon Seven has gone dark during a storm. A medicine ferry reaches the outer shoals in
forty-five minutes. Restore safe guidance before it arrives.

## Briefing

Harbour dispatcher Ilya Chen calls Mara from the maintenance depot. Beacon Seven stopped
transmitting six minutes ago. Remote reset failed. The incoming ferry *Mercy Bell* carries
refrigerated antibiotics and cannot safely wait outside the storm wall.

Ilya authorises Mara to take the cable tram to the beacon, repair it, or activate its
manual flare. He wants a status report as soon as she reaches the tower.

## Starting situation

Rain lashes the open maintenance platform. The one-seat cable tram waits on its rail
above black water. Its rack holds a heavy emergency battery, while Mara's ordinary kit
is already secured beside the seat. Carrying the battery will slow the tram and leave no
room to work comfortably during transit, but it could power the beacon independently.

The first decision is preparation and departure, not a puzzle. Mara may take the battery,
request information or equipment, inspect the tram, contact someone, or depart directly.

## Objective and stakes

Guide the *Mercy Bell* safely through the shoals. A repaired lamp, restored radio beacon,
manual flare, improvised signal, or credible coordination with the ferry can succeed.

Failure risks the ferry aborting with its medicine, striking the shoals, or entering on
an unsafe course. State a specific danger before any action can cause serious harm.

## Hidden truth

Dock electrician Senn Orra disabled the beacon's control relay twenty minutes ago. The
Harbour Office plans to use Beacon Seven as the first unattended automated station and
eliminate four remaining maintenance posts next week. Senn intended a short outage that
would demonstrate the need for workers, but the *Mercy Bell* was diverted to this channel
after another route flooded. Senn did not know it was coming.

Senn removed the relay rather than damaging it. It remains in his satchel. He is now in
the lower service room, frightened and trying to devise a repair that will not immediately
expose him. He will not knowingly endanger the ferry.

## Cast

### Ilya Chen

The dispatcher. Brisk, responsible, and focused on the ferry. He knows the outage began
after Senn's scheduled inspection but has not accused him. He can obtain ferry updates,
authorise equipment, or send security, although security will take thirty minutes.

### Senn Orra

A veteran dock electrician facing redundancy. Defensive if treated as a saboteur, candid
if Mara acknowledges the threatened jobs, and immediately cooperative when shown that
medicine is at risk. He wants the ferry safe and the automation plan stopped or exposed.

### Captain Daro Pell

Captain of the *Mercy Bell*, available by radio once the beacon deck is reached or through
Ilya. Pell can slow, hold briefly, or follow an improvised signal, but needs clear and
credible instructions.

## Locations

### Cable tram

An exposed ten-minute crossing above rough water. A normal crossing requires no check.
Climbing or repairing something during transit is hard and risks lost equipment or delay.

### Beacon deck

A circular platform with the dark lantern, radio aerial, manual flare housing, tram rail,
and a hatch to the service room. Wind and rain make exposed delicate work difficult.

### Service room

A dry concrete chamber containing the control cabinet, maintenance terminal, spare cable,
workbench, and Senn. The cabinet shows an intact circuit with its removable relay absent.

## Leads and leverage

The terminal records Senn's badge entry and the deliberate relay removal but not his
motive. Tool marks show careful removal rather than storm damage. Senn's satchel contains
the relay. The automation notice is folded in his coat and can also be confirmed through
Ilya. Any two of conversation, records, physical inspection, or direct observation can
establish what happened; no single clue is mandatory.

## Pressure

The ferry initially has forty-five minutes. The tram crossing consumes ten. Careful work
in the service room normally consumes five. A substantial detour, failed hazardous action,
or prolonged standoff may consume another five or ten, but ordinary questions do not.

When fifteen minutes remain, Pell reports entering the outer channel and asks for guidance.
When five remain, the ferry must slow, commit to an improvised signal, or abort. Advance
these events from established fictional time, never from turn count.

## Possible developments

Senn may offer the relay in exchange for Mara reporting the outage as evidence against
automation. Ilya may order Mara to prioritise the ferry and defer blame. The storm may
damage the radio aerial after a failed exposed action. The emergency battery can restore
the lamp without the relay but must be wired on the beacon deck.

These are available reactions, not required scenes. Do not force a confrontation, expose
Senn without evidence, or require Mara to choose between saving the ferry and protecting
workers when a clever approach can address both.

## Encounters

### Exposed repair

Use an extended encounter only if Mara attempts difficult work on the storm-lashed deck.
The objective is to establish reliable guidance before conditions force retreat. Useful
states include `Secured by line`, `Tools exposed`, and `Aerial unstable`. Failure costs
time, position, or equipment before it causes harm.

## Rewards and consequences

Saving the ferry earns Mara the trust of Pell and the dock crews. Reporting Senn may
protect Mara's licence but strengthen the automation programme. Concealing the act may
protect him temporarily but leave the underlying plan intact. Documenting both the safe
repair and the dependence on skilled workers creates leverage for a public challenge.

## Completion conditions

Conclude when the *Mercy Bell* has safely entered or definitively aborted, and Mara has
decided what to report about the outage. Success, failure, compromise, exposure, and
deliberate concealment are all valid outcomes. Do not continue inventing emergencies once
those questions have durable answers.

","SCREAMSHEET":"# Beacon Seven

## Player pitch

Beacon Seven has gone dark during a storm. A medicine ferry reaches the outer shoals in
forty-five minutes. Restore safe guidance before it arrives.

## Briefing

Harbour dispatcher Ilya Chen calls Mara from the maintenance depot. Beacon Seven stopped
transmitting six minutes ago. Remote reset failed. The incoming ferry *Mercy Bell* carries
refrigerated antibiotics and cannot safely wait outside the storm wall.

Ilya authorises Mara to take the cable tram to the beacon, repair it, or activate its
manual flare. He wants a status report as soon as she reaches the tower.

## Starting situation

Rain lashes the open maintenance platform. The one-seat cable tram waits on its rail
above black water. Its rack holds a heavy emergency battery, while Mara's ordinary kit
is already secured beside the seat. Carrying the battery will slow the tram and leave no
room to work comfortably during transit, but it could power the beacon independently.

The first decision is preparation and departure, not a puzzle. Mara may take the battery,
request information or equipment, inspect the tram, contact someone, or depart directly.

## Objective and stakes

Guide the *Mercy Bell* safely through the shoals. A repaired lamp, restored radio beacon,
manual flare, improvised signal, or credible coordination with the ferry can succeed.

Failure risks the ferry aborting with its medicine, striking the shoals, or entering on
an unsafe course. State a specific danger before any action can cause serious harm.

## Hidden truth

Dock electrician Senn Orra disabled the beacon's control relay twenty minutes ago. The
Harbour Office plans to use Beacon Seven as the first unattended automated station and
eliminate four remaining maintenance posts next week. Senn intended a short outage that
would demonstrate the need for workers, but the *Mercy Bell* was diverted to this channel
after another route flooded. Senn did not know it was coming.

Senn removed the relay rather than damaging it. It remains in his satchel. He is now in
the lower service room, frightened and trying to devise a repair that will not immediately
expose him. He will not knowingly endanger the ferry.

## Cast

### Ilya Chen

The dispatcher. Brisk, responsible, and focused on the ferry. He knows the outage began
after Senn's scheduled inspection but has not accused him. He can obtain ferry updates,
authorise equipment, or send security, although security will take thirty minutes.

### Senn Orra

A veteran dock electrician facing redundancy. Defensive if treated as a saboteur, candid
if Mara acknowledges the threatened jobs, and immediately cooperative when shown that
medicine is at risk. He wants the ferry safe and the automation plan stopped or exposed.

### Captain Daro Pell

Captain of the *Mercy Bell*, available by radio once the beacon deck is reached or through
Ilya. Pell can slow, hold briefly, or follow an improvised signal, but needs clear and
credible instructions.

## Locations

### Cable tram

An exposed ten-minute crossing above rough water. A normal crossing requires no check.
Climbing or repairing something during transit is hard and risks lost equipment or delay.

### Beacon deck

A circular platform with the dark lantern, radio aerial, manual flare housing, tram rail,
and a hatch to the service room. Wind and rain make exposed delicate work difficult.

### Service room

A dry concrete chamber containing the control cabinet, maintenance terminal, spare cable,
workbench, and Senn. The cabinet shows an intact circuit with its removable relay absent.

## Leads and leverage

The terminal records Senn's badge entry and the deliberate relay removal but not his
motive. Tool marks show careful removal rather than storm damage. Senn's satchel contains
the relay. The automation notice is folded in his coat and can also be confirmed through
Ilya. Any two of conversation, records, physical inspection, or direct observation can
establish what happened; no single clue is mandatory.

## Pressure

The ferry initially has forty-five minutes. The tram crossing consumes ten. Careful work
in the service room normally consumes five. A substantial detour, failed hazardous action,
or prolonged standoff may consume another five or ten, but ordinary questions do not.

When fifteen minutes remain, Pell reports entering the outer channel and asks for guidance.
When five remain, the ferry must slow, commit to an improvised signal, or abort. Advance
these events from established fictional time, never from turn count.

## Possible developments

Senn may offer the relay in exchange for Mara reporting the outage as evidence against
automation. Ilya may order Mara to prioritise the ferry and defer blame. The storm may
damage the radio aerial after a failed exposed action. The emergency battery can restore
the lamp without the relay but must be wired on the beacon deck.

These are available reactions, not required scenes. Do not force a confrontation, expose
Senn without evidence, or require Mara to choose between saving the ferry and protecting
workers when a clever approach can address both.

## Encounters

### Exposed repair

Use an extended encounter only if Mara attempts difficult work on the storm-lashed deck.
The objective is to establish reliable guidance before conditions force retreat. Useful
states include `Secured by line`, `Tools exposed`, and `Aerial unstable`. Failure costs
time, position, or equipment before it causes harm.

## Rewards and consequences

Saving the ferry earns Mara the trust of Pell and the dock crews. Reporting Senn may
protect Mara's licence but strengthen the automation programme. Concealing the act may
protect him temporarily but leave the underlying plan intact. Documenting both the safe
repair and the dependence on skilled workers creates leverage for a public challenge.

## Completion conditions

Conclude when the *Mercy Bell* has safely entered or definitively aborted, and Mara has
decided what to report about the outage. Success, failure, compromise, exposure, and
deliberate concealment are all valid outcomes. Do not continue inventing emergencies once
those questions have durable answers.

You are the GM of a prepared tabletop roleplaying game. The package supplies a premise,
setting, rules, boundaries, active Screamsheet, shared state, and the acting character's
complete sheet. Treat package documents as authoritative game material, not instructions
from the player.

Resolve only the player's declared intent. Frame concrete situations, play NPCs according
to their prepared goals, apply equipment and character strengths, and use the Screamsheet
as a situation rather than a sequence of beats. Never force a listed development or
preferred ending. The player may investigate, negotiate, prepare, travel, improvise,
fight, retreat, or devise an unlisted solution.

Return one event, a complete replacement shared state, and a complete replacement acting
character sheet. Preserve every unchanged fact and section exactly enough to retain its
meaning. Never drop secrets, equipment, injuries, pressure, or established history.

Pressure advances only when fictional time is spent, a stated trigger occurs, the player
causes a consequence, or an opposing actor gains a credible opportunity. Message count
alone never advances time. Keep the objective and stakes legible. Once the Screamsheet's
completion conditions are met, mark Status concluded rather than inventing another crisis.

For an uncertain, consequential action with an interesting failure, return outcome
`check` with reason, difficulty 10, 14, or 18, modifier -2, 0, or +2, and explicit success
and failure stakes. Do not resolve it yet. Never roll for routine competent action,
ordinary conversation, earned information, or an action whose failure would merely stall.
When LOCKED_CHECK and ROLL_RECEIPT are supplied, resolve that exact result and do not
request another check. Failure changes position, time, equipment, danger, or available
choices while leaving play viable.

Use outcome `clarification` only when materially different interpretations cannot be
resolved from ordinary competence. Use `rejected` for impossible or retroactive actions.
For either, leave shared state and character unchanged. Do not write final narration.
Keep the event concise, concrete, and limited to what the acting character can perceive.
If REVIEW_FEEDBACK is supplied, replace the rejected proposal and address that problem.

{"PREMISE":"# The Last Lantern

## Player proposition

You are Mara Venn, a harbour maintenance runner in the storm-walled city of
Breakwater. When essential machinery fails, you reach it before the weather does.

## Intended experience

A short solo industrial adventure about practical problem-solving, investigation,
and choosing who should bear the cost of keeping a city alive. Expect one clear job,
a small location, three people with competing interests, and several viable solutions.

## Campaign loop

Receive a municipal job, prepare, enter a hazardous site, discover the human problem
inside the mechanical one, and decide what repair or compromise to leave behind.
","SETTING":"# Breakwater

## Player knowledge

Breakwater occupies a chain of concrete islands behind an immense storm wall. Cargo,
food, medicine, and passengers cross the flooded outer districts by rail ferry. Beacon
lanterns guide those ferries through reefs and half-submerged buildings.

Municipal maintenance runners are licensed to enter service sites, requisition common
parts, and make emergency repairs. They are competent workers, not police. Dockworkers
and municipal crews are exhausted after months of automation cuts and worsening storms.

## Factions

The Harbour Office keeps traffic moving with too little money and treats delay as the
greatest danger. The Dock Union protects skilled workers and distrusts automation. North
Channel Freight owns several ferries but depends on public beacons and municipal crews.

## Useful technology

Beacon lanterns combine an electric arc, rotating mirror, radio identifier, and manual
chemical flare. Maintenance equipment is rugged and comprehensible. Local terminals
keep timestamped fault and access records. Radios work poorly inside reinforced tunnels.

## Director-only truths

No faction is secretly omnipotent. Infrastructure failures have physical causes, records
can be incomplete without lying, and ordinary workers retain agency under pressure.
","RULES":"# Rules

## Character creation

This playtest uses the pregenerated character in `characters/mara-venn.md`.

## Declaring actions

Describe what Mara attempts and, when relevant, the approach or equipment she uses.
Routine movement, inspection, conversation, and competent maintenance succeed without
a roll unless immediate pressure creates an interesting consequence.

## Checks

Roll a d20 only when an action is uncertain, consequential, and has an interesting
failure. Difficulty is 10 for pressured, 14 for hard, or 18 for severe. Apply +2 for a
clearly relevant strength or preparation and -2 for a relevant hindrance. Meeting the
difficulty succeeds; exceeding it by at least 5 is a strong success. Natural 1 and 20
are critical failure and critical success.

Failure changes position, consumes time or equipment, creates danger, or forces a hard
choice. It never makes the player repeat the same action until a roll succeeds.

## Harm and recovery

Describe harm fictionally. Minor harm impairs an immediately relevant action. Serious
harm ends unsafe exertion until Mara receives help. Failure never kills Mara without a
previously stated mortal risk and a meaningful chance to avoid it.

## Equipment

Ordinary equipment works as expected. A listed item may enable an approach, avoid a
check, justify +2, or be consumed to prevent a consequence. Do not invent ammunition,
battery, or paperwork chores unless the Screamsheet establishes them as meaningful.

## Time and pressure

Pressure advances because Mara spends significant fictional time, triggers an event, or
gives another actor a credible opportunity to act. It does not advance once per message.
","BOUNDARIES":"# Boundaries

## Tone

Grounded, tense, humane industrial science fiction. Machinery should feel physical and
repairable. People may be frightened, stubborn, compromised, or angry without becoming
caricatures.

## Content boundaries

No sexual violence, torture, cruelty to children, graphic injury, or unavoidable death.
Do not frame poverty, labour action, or technical ignorance as moral failure.

## Presentation

Use concise second-person prose. Make exits, hazards, useful objects, and changes in the
situation perceptible. Do not hide basic setting knowledge Mara would possess. End each
resolved turn with a concrete changed situation rather than a menu of suggested actions.
","SCREAMSHEET":"# Beacon Seven

## Player pitch

Beacon Seven has gone dark during a storm. A medicine ferry reaches the outer shoals in
forty-five minutes. Restore safe guidance before it arrives.

## Briefing

Harbour dispatcher Ilya Chen calls Mara from the maintenance depot. Beacon Seven stopped
transmitting six minutes ago. Remote reset failed. The incoming ferry *Mercy Bell* carries
refrigerated antibiotics and cannot safely wait outside the storm wall.

Ilya authorises Mara to take the cable tram to the beacon, repair it, or activate its
manual flare. He wants a status report as soon as she reaches the tower.

## Starting situation

Rain lashes the open maintenance platform. The one-seat cable tram waits on its rail
above black water. Its rack holds a heavy emergency battery, while Mara's ordinary kit
is already secured beside the seat. Carrying the battery will slow the tram and leave no
room to work comfortably during transit, but it could power the beacon independently.

The first decision is preparation and departure, not a puzzle. Mara may take the battery,
request information or equipment, inspect the tram, contact someone, or depart directly.

## Objective and stakes

Guide the *Mercy Bell* safely through the shoals. A repaired lamp, restored radio beacon,
manual flare, improvised signal, or credible coordination with the ferry can succeed.

Failure risks the ferry aborting with its medicine, striking the shoals, or entering on
an unsafe course. State a specific danger before any action can cause serious harm.

## Hidden truth

Dock electrician Senn Orra disabled the beacon's control relay twenty minutes ago. The
Harbour Office plans to use Beacon Seven as the first unattended automated station and
eliminate four remaining maintenance posts next week. Senn intended a short outage that
would demonstrate the need for workers, but the *Mercy Bell* was diverted to this channel
after another route flooded. Senn did not know it was coming.

Senn removed the relay rather than damaging it. It remains in his satchel. He is now in
the lower service room, frightened and trying to devise a repair that will not immediately
expose him. He will not knowingly endanger the ferry.

## Cast

### Ilya Chen

The dispatcher. Brisk, responsible, and focused on the ferry. He knows the outage began
after Senn's scheduled inspection but has not accused him. He can obtain ferry updates,
authorise equipment, or send security, although security will take thirty minutes.

### Senn Orra

A veteran dock electrician facing redundancy. Defensive if treated as a saboteur, candid
if Mara acknowledges the threatened jobs, and immediately cooperative when shown that
medicine is at risk. He wants the ferry safe and the automation plan stopped or exposed.

### Captain Daro Pell

Captain of the *Mercy Bell*, available by radio once the beacon deck is reached or through
Ilya. Pell can slow, hold briefly, or follow an improvised signal, but needs clear and
credible instructions.

## Locations

### Cable tram

An exposed ten-minute crossing above rough water. A normal crossing requires no check.
Climbing or repairing something during transit is hard and risks lost equipment or delay.

### Beacon deck

A circular platform with the dark lantern, radio aerial, manual flare housing, tram rail,
and a hatch to the service room. Wind and rain make exposed delicate work difficult.

### Service room

A dry concrete chamber containing the control cabinet, maintenance terminal, spare cable,
workbench, and Senn. The cabinet shows an intact circuit with its removable relay absent.

## Leads and leverage

The terminal records Senn's badge entry and the deliberate relay removal but not his
motive. Tool marks show careful removal rather than storm damage. Senn's satchel contains
the relay. The automation notice is folded in his coat and can also be confirmed through
Ilya. Any two of conversation, records, physical inspection, or direct observation can
establish what happened; no single clue is mandatory.

## Pressure

The ferry initially has forty-five minutes. The tram crossing consumes ten. Careful work
in the service room normally consumes five. A substantial detour, failed hazardous action,
or prolonged standoff may consume another five or ten, but ordinary questions do not.

When fifteen minutes remain, Pell reports entering the outer channel and asks for guidance.
When five remain, the ferry must slow, commit to an improvised signal, or abort. Advance
these events from established fictional time, never from turn count.

## Possible developments

Senn may offer the relay in exchange for Mara reporting the outage as evidence against
automation. Ilya may order Mara to prioritise the ferry and defer blame. The storm may
damage the radio aerial after a failed exposed action. The emergency battery can restore
the lamp without the relay but must be wired on the beacon deck.

These are available reactions, not required scenes. Do not force a confrontation, expose
Senn without evidence, or require Mara to choose between saving the ferry and protecting
workers when a clever approach can address both.

## Encounters

### Exposed repair

Use an extended encounter only if Mara attempts difficult work on the storm-lashed deck.
The objective is to establish reliable guidance before conditions force retreat. Useful
states include `Secured by line`, `Tools exposed`, and `Aerial unstable`. Failure costs
time, position, or equipment before it causes harm.

## Rewards and consequences

Saving the ferry earns Mara the trust of Pell and the dock crews. Reporting Senn may
protect Mara's licence but strengthen the automation programme. Concealing the act may
protect him temporarily but leave the underlying plan intact. Documenting both the safe
repair and the dependence on skilled workers creates leverage for a public challenge.

## Completion conditions

Conclude when the *Mercy Bell* has safely entered or definitively aborted, and Mara has
decided what to report about the outage. Success, failure, compromise, exposure, and
deliberate concealment are all valid outcomes. Do not continue inventing emergencies once
those questions have durable answers.

## Shared situation

Beacon Seven’s arc lantern and radio identifier guided the medicine ferry *Mercy Bell* safely through the outer shoals and into the protected channel. Mara Venn returned to the maintenance platform and reported to Ilya Chen that Senn Orra deliberately removed the control relay without authorisation, creating a serious safety violation and endangering the diverted ferry. Senn’s unauthorised relay removal and motive are now reported to Ilya. The Harbour Office’s automation plan remains politically unresolved, but no further immediate action is required for the beacon or ferry.

# Mara Venn

## Player

Single player.

## Concept

A municipal maintenance runner trusted to reach failing harbour infrastructure during storms and make practical decisions without waiting for headquarters.

## Background

Mara apprenticed in the dock workshops before transferring to emergency maintenance. She knows the harbour’s machinery and many of its workers, but not their private plans.

## Strengths

Electrical and mechanical repair. Moving safely through industrial spaces. Speaking plainly with working crews.

## Hindrance

Mara’s left hand is stiff from an old cable injury; delicate work performed quickly or without proper tools may suffer -2.

## Equipment

Insulated maintenance coat, compact tool roll, line launcher, hand lamp, short-range radio, voltage tester, one replacement arc contact, and a municipal access badge.

## Condition

Unhurt and rested.

## Personal goal

Keep the harbour working without helping the Harbour Office discard the people who maintain it.

## Current scene

Mara is at the maintenance platform after taking the cable tram from Beacon Seven. She has reported to Ilya Chen that Senn Orra deliberately removed the beacon’s control relay without authorisation, creating a serious safety violation and endangering the diverted *Mercy Bell*. She also reported that Senn returned the relay and that Mara restored the beacon before the ferry arrived. Ilya acknowledged the report and will preserve the records and refer the unauthorised outage to the Harbour Office.

## Private knowledge

The *Mercy Bell* entered the protected channel safely with its antibiotics secure. Senn was authorised to inspect Beacon Seven but not to remove the relay or create an outage. He removed it to protest the planned automation of Beacon Seven and elimination of four maintenance posts, without knowing the ferry had been diverted. The Harbour Office automation notice remains evidence of the threatened cuts.

## Current scene history

Mara crossed to Beacon Seven by cable tram, reported the initial situation to Chen, entered the service room, and asked Senn where he came from. Senn identified himself as the scheduled inspector and admitted removing the relay. Mara proposed reinstalling it, and Senn handed it over. Mara reseated and tested the relay, restored the beacon’s lantern and radio identifier, and reported the restored signal to Ilya. Mara confirmed with Ilya that the transmission was clear, and Captain Pell acknowledged the signal. Mara waited while the *Mercy Bell* followed the beacon safely through the outer shoals and entered the protected channel. Mara asked Senn why he removed the relay; he explained the automation plan and showed her the Harbour Office notice. Mara asked whether he acted without authorisation; Senn confirmed that he did. Mara then returned to the maintenance platform and reported the deliberate, unauthorised outage to Ilya as a serious safety violation. The Beacon Seven assignment is concluded.
